summary:
Sol Survivors is a free browser game for kids aged 7–12. One to three players crash-land on Mars in Jezero Crater and have until the end of Sol 12 to repair their base and fly home. Each player takes a job: Botanist, Builder or Pilot. Each job can do things the others can’t, so the crew has to cooperate. They repair five broken machines, starting with MOXIE, the air-making machine. They also balance Food, Oxygen and Health while dust storms, solar flares and freezing nights hit the base. Eight short mini-games, such as splitting CO₂ and aiming a laser at Earth, turn each repair into hands-on play. Each win ends with a real science fact.

It tackles the challenge by making every choice cost something. Fixing power, growing food and keeping air breathable compete for limited time and supplies. Mechanics and numbers come from NASA data where it exists, covering radiation, real solar flares, Martian sol length and signal delay. The game labels each number as “REAL” or “GAME” (simplified), so nothing is passed off as data it isn’t. Random world seeds make every run different, and nobody dies. Passing out just means waking in the medbay, so failure teaches without punishing.
